abstract.def: Art that simplifies, exaggerates or rearranges what things really look like, so you may only partly recognize the subject (or not at all). The word describes how far an image has moved away from a photo-like copy.
abstract.think: Think of a stick figure or an emoji face: you know it is a person, but it is not trying to look real.
abstract.seen: No. 132 Improvisation 28; No. 136 Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow; No. 145 Woman, I.

all-over composition.def: A composition with no single focal point or center of interest: marks and shapes spread evenly across the surface, right to the edges. It is linked with Jackson Pollock but also fits Lam’s The Jungle and Kngwarreye’s Earth’s Creation.
all-over composition.think: Like wallpaper or a field of grass: your eye has no one place to land.
all-over composition.seen: No. 142 The Jungle; No. 234 Earth’s Creation.

analogous colors.def: Colors that sit next to each other on the color wheel, such as yellow, yellow-orange and orange. Used together they feel calm and unified rather than clashing.
analogous colors.think: Think of a sunset that goes from yellow to orange to red with no sharp jumps.

aniconic.def: Avoiding pictures of people, animals or gods, especially in a religious setting. Instead the art uses writing, patterns and plants. Common in Islamic religious spaces and in very early Buddhist art, where the Buddha was shown only by symbols such as a footprint or an empty throne.
aniconic.think: Think of a mosque wall covered in beautiful writing and patterns but with no faces anywhere.
aniconic.seen: No. 185 Dome of the Rock; No. 187 Folio from a Qur’an; No. 192 Great Stupa at Sanchi.

anthropomorphic.def: Shaped like a human or given human features. Used for objects, animals or gods made to look partly or fully human.
anthropomorphic.seen: No. 6 Anthropomorphic stele; No. 217 Female deity (Nukuoro).

arbitrary color.def: Color chosen for feeling or effect rather than to match real life, like a green face or a red sky. Common in modern art from the 1880s on.
arbitrary color.think: Think of an Instagram filter that turns a sky purple on purpose.
arbitrary color.seen: No. 133 SelfPortrait as a Soldier; No. 123 Where Do We Come From?.

archaic smile.def: The slight, fixed smile on Greek statues made around 600 to 480 B.C.E. It probably did not mean happiness; it was a way to make the face look alive.
archaic smile.think: Think of a polite school-photo smile that stays the same no matter what.
archaic smile.seen: No. 27 Anavysos Kouros; No. 28 Peplos Kore.

asymmetry.def: When the two halves of a picture or object do not match. Artists still balance an asymmetrical work by setting, say, one big shape against several small ones. Also called asymmetrical balance.
asymmetry.think: Think of a seesaw with one adult near the middle balancing two kids at the far end.
asymmetry.seen: No. 101 The Swing; No. 211 Great Wave; No. 210 White and Red Plum Blossoms.

atmospheric perspective.def: A way to show distance by making faraway things paler, bluer, hazier and less detailed, the way mountains look on the horizon. Also called aerial perspective.
atmospheric perspective.think: Think of looking at hills on a hazy day: the farther ones fade to pale blue.
atmospheric perspective.seen: No. 83 Hunters in the Snow; No. 118 The Valley of Mexico; No. 201 Travelers among Mountains and Streams.
atmospheric perspective.see: linear perspective, background, space, horizon line.

axis.def: An imaginary straight line running through the center of a body, object or building, around which its parts are arranged. A standing figure usually has a vertical axis; in contrapposto that axis bends.
axis.think: Think of the spine of a book or the pole on a merry-go-round.

background.def: The part of a picture that seems farthest from you, behind the main figures.
background.think: Think of the scenery behind actors on a stage.
background.seen: No. 83 Hunters in the Snow; No. 201 Travelers among Mountains and Streams.

balance.def: How the visual ‘weight’ of shapes, colors and objects is spread around a work so it feels stable instead of tipping to one side. It can be symmetrical, asymmetrical or radial.
balance.think: Think of arranging furniture so one side of a room does not feel crowded.

biomorphic.def: Shapes that look like living things: soft, rounded and curvy rather than geometric, though not any particular plant or animal.

bird’s-eye view.def: A view from high above, looking down on a scene as a bird would. It lets an artist show a lot of ground at once, such as a whole battle or city.
bird’s-eye view.think: Think of a drone shot or a Google Maps satellite view.
bird’s-eye view.seen: No. 94 Screen with the Siege of Belgrade; No. 118 The Valley of Mexico; No. 203 Night Attack on the Sanjô Palace.

canon of proportions.def: A set of rules for the ideal size of each body part compared with the others, used so every figure looks ‘correct’. The Greek sculptor Polykleitos wrote one; Egyptian artists used a grid system.
canon of proportions.think: Think of a recipe for the perfect body: the head is one part, the body is seven parts, and so on.
canon of proportions.seen: No. 34 Doryphoros; No. 18 King Menkaura and queen.

chiaroscuro.def: Using strong contrasts of light and dark to make figures look rounded and solid. Italian for ‘light-dark’.
chiaroscuro.think: Think of a face lit by one lamp in a dark room: one side bright, the other in shadow.
chiaroscuro.seen: No. 100 A Philosopher Giving a Lecture on the Orrery; No. 92 Woman Holding a Balance; No. 85 Calling of Saint Matthew.

closed form.def: A sculpture or figure that stays compact, with arms and legs held close to the body so it reads as one solid block. The opposite of open form.
closed form.think: Think of someone sitting hugging their knees.
closed form.seen: No. 18 King Menkaura and queen; No. 129 The Kiss (Brancusi); No. 15 Seated scribe.

color.def: What we see when light reflects off a surface. When describing color, people talk about hue (its name), value (how light or dark) and saturation (how strong or dull).
color.think: Think of picking a paint chip: you choose the color family, then how light and how bright.

color wheel.def: A circle that arranges colors in rainbow order so you can see which colors are related. Opposite colors are complementary; neighbors are analogous.
color wheel.think: Think of a pizza where each slice is a color.
color wheel.see: primary colors, secondary colors, complementary colors, analogous colors.

complementary colors.def: Pairs of colors opposite each other on the color wheel: red and green, blue and orange, yellow and purple. Placed side by side they make each other look stronger.
complementary colors.think: Think of Christmas red and green, or a sports jersey in blue and orange.
complementary colors.seen: No. 131 Goldfish; No. 120 The Starry Night.

composite view.def: Showing different parts of one body from their most recognizable angles at the same time: head in profile, eye from the front, shoulders from the front, legs in profile. Common in Egyptian and Near Eastern art. Also called twisted perspective.
composite view.think: Think of a figure built from the clearest photo of each body part, glued together.
composite view.seen: No. 13 Palette of King Narmer; No. 24 Last judgment of Hu-Nefer; No. 2 Great Hall of the Bulls.

composition.def: How everything in a work is arranged: where figures sit, how big they are, which way lines run. Good composition guides your eye where the artist wants it.
composition.think: Think of how a photographer frames a shot before pressing the button.
composition.see: balance, focal point, pyramidal composition, unity.

continuous narrative.def: Showing several moments of one story in a single picture or band, often with the same person appearing more than once.
continuous narrative.think: Think of a comic strip with the panel borders removed.
continuous narrative.seen: No. 50 Vienna Genesis; No. 59 Bayeux Tapestry; No. 203 Night Attack on the Sanjô Palace; No. 45 Forum of Trajan (Column).

contour line.def: The outline that marks the outer edge of a shape or figure. A strong contour makes shapes look crisp and clear.
contour line.think: Think of a coloring-book outline before you fill it in.
contour line.seen: No. 1 Apollo 11 Stones; No. 107 La Grande Odalisque; No. 33 Niobides Krater.

contrapposto.def: A relaxed standing pose where the weight rests on one leg, so the hips tilt one way and the shoulders tilt the other, giving the body a gentle S-curve. Invented by the Greeks to make statues look alive.
contrapposto.think: Think of how you stand while waiting in line, leaning on one leg.
contrapposto.seen: No. 34 Doryphoros; No. 69 David (Donatello); No. 43 Augustus of Prima Porta; No. 104 George Washington.
contrapposto.see: axis, idealized, in the round, canon of proportions.

contrast.def: A strong difference between two things placed together: light and dark, rough and smooth, big and small, bright and dull. Contrast grabs attention.
contrast.think: Think of white text on a black screen.

convention.def: An accepted, repeated way of showing something in a particular culture, even if it is not realistic. Viewers in that culture understand it automatically.
convention.think: Think of how a heart shape means love even though real hearts do not look like that.
convention.seen: No. 13 Palette of King Narmer; No. 24 Last judgment of Hu-Nefer.

cool colors.def: Blues, greens and purples. They feel calm or cold and tend to seem to sink back into the distance.
cool colors.think: Think of ice, water and shade.
cool colors.see: warm colors, color wheel, atmospheric perspective.

cropping.def: Cutting off part of a scene at the edge of the frame, so figures or objects are only partly shown. It makes an image feel like a quick snapshot.
cropping.think: Think of a phone photo where someone’s arm is cut off by the edge.

curvilinear.def: Made of curving, flowing lines rather than straight ones.

diagonal.def: A slanted line or direction. Diagonals feel active and unstable compared with calm horizontals and verticals.
diagonal.think: Think of a falling tree versus a standing one.
diagonal.seen: No. 101 The Swing; No. 108 Liberty Leading the People; No. 211 Great Wave.

diminution of scale.def: Making things smaller the farther away they are supposed to be. One of the basic tricks for showing depth.
diminution of scale.think: Think of a road whose cars get tinier as it stretches away.
diminution of scale.seen: No. 83 Hunters in the Snow; No. 76 School of Athens.

distortion.def: Stretching, twisting or exaggerating forms on purpose, usually to show emotion or a new idea rather than accuracy.
distortion.seen: No. 122 The Scream; No. 145 Woman, I ; No. 126 Les Demoiselles d’Avignon.

dramatic lighting.def: Strong, focused light that throws some areas into bright highlight and leaves others in deep shadow, raising the emotional temperature of a scene.
dramatic lighting.think: Think of a stage spotlight in a dark theater.
dramatic lighting.seen: No. 85 Calling of Saint Matthew; No. 100 A Philosopher Giving a Lecture on the Orrery; No. 111 Slave Ship.

dynamic.def: Full of energy and suggested movement, usually through diagonals, twisting bodies or swirling lines. The opposite of static.
dynamic.think: Think of a sports photo caught mid-jump.
dynamic.seen: No. 37 Winged Victory of Samothrace; No. 38 Great Altar of Zeus and Athena at Pergamon; No. 211 Great Wave.

elongation.def: Stretching a figure or body part longer than normal, usually for elegance or spiritual effect.
elongation.think: Think of a fashion sketch with impossibly long legs.
elongation.seen: No. 107 La Grande Odalisque; No. 78 Entombment of Christ.

emphasis.def: The way an artist makes one part stand out more than the rest, using light, color, size, placement or lines that point to it.
emphasis.think: Think of bold text in a paragraph.
emphasis.seen: No. 85 Calling of Saint Matthew; No. 73 Last Supper.

expressive.def: Made to show strong feeling. An expressive work uses color, line or distortion to make you feel something rather than to record what things look like.
expressive.think: Think of the difference between a weather report and a breakup song.
expressive.seen: No. 122 The Scream; No. 62 Röttgen Pietà; No. 133 Self-Portrait as a Soldier.

figurative.def: Art that shows recognizable figures, especially people or animals. Often used as the opposite of abstract or nonrepresentational.
figurative.think: If you can point at it and say ‘that’s a person’, it is figurative.

figure-ground relationship.def: How the main shapes (the figure) stand out from what is behind them (the ground). Some works play with this so you are not sure which is which.
figure-ground relationship.think: Think of the classic picture that can be read as either a vase or two faces.

finish.def: How smooth or rough the final surface is. A high finish hides brushstrokes completely; a loose finish leaves them visible.
finish.think: Think of a glossy car paint job versus a hand-painted fence.
finish.seen: No. 107 La Grande Odalisque; No. 120 The Starry Night.

flatness.def: When a picture looks deliberately twodimensional, with little shading or depth, so you notice the surface. Many modern painters chose flatness on purpose.
flatness.think: Think of a cartoon sticker instead of a 3D movie.
flatness.seen: No. 115 Olympia; No. 131 Goldfish; No. 210 White and Red Plum Blossoms.

focal point.def: The spot your eye goes to first, usually the most important part of the work.
focal point.think: Think of the bullseye on a target.
focal point.seen: No. 73 Last Supper; No. 103 The Oath of the Horatii.

foreground.def: The part of a picture that seems closest to you, at the bottom or front of the scene.
foreground.think: Think of the people standing right in front of the camera.
foreground.seen: No. 83 Hunters in the Snow; No. 201 Travelers among Mountains and Streams.

foreshortening.def: Drawing something that points toward or away from you so it looks squashed and shorter, which makes it seem to stick out in space.
foreshortening.think: Think of a selfie with your arm stretched toward the camera: your hand looks huge and your arm almost disappears.
foreshortening.seen: No. 75 Sistine Chapel ceiling; No. 82 Il Gesù ceiling.
foreshortening.see: linear perspective, illusionism, di sotto in sù.

form.def: A shape that has (or looks like it has) three dimensions: height, width and depth. In art talk ‘form’ can also mean all the visual parts of a work together, as opposed to its subject.
form.think: A circle is a shape; a ball is a form.

formal analysis.def: Describing and explaining a work by looking only at its visual parts: line, color, shape, space, texture, composition and so on, before talking about meaning.
formal analysis.think: Think of reviewing a car by its looks and build before asking who made it or why.

fragmentation.def: Breaking forms into pieces, planes or shards, often reassembled in a new way. Central to Cubism.
fragmentation.think: Think of a reflection in a shattered mirror.
fragmentation.seen: No. 130 The Portuguese; No. 126 Les Demoiselles d’Avignon.

frontal.def: Facing straight out at the viewer, square to the front. Frontal figures often look formal, stiff and powerful.
frontal.seen: No. 18 King Menkaura and queen; No. 54 Theotokos and Child; No. 14 Votive figures from Eshnunna; No. 51 San Vitale.

gaze.def: Where figures are looking, and how they look at us or at each other. Art historians also use ‘the gaze’ to talk about who is doing the looking and who is being looked at.
gaze.think: Think of how awkward it is when someone in a photo stares straight into the lens at you.

geometric.def: Made of regular, measurable shapes such as squares, circles, triangles and straight lines. The opposite of organic.
geometric.think: Think of shapes you could draw with a ruler and compass.
geometric.seen: No. 136 Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow; No. 162 All-T’oqapu tunic; No. 5 Beaker with ibex motifs; No. 55 Lindisfarne Gospels.

gesture.def: The pose or hand movement of a figure that communicates something, like pointing, blessing or reaching.
gesture.think: Think of a referee’s signals: you understand them without words.
gesture.seen: No. 76 School of Athens; No. 85 Calling of Saint Matthew; No. 103 The Oath of the Horatii.

grid.def: A network of crossing horizontal and vertical lines. Artists use grids to arrange a composition, to keep proportions, or as the look of the work itself.
grid.think: Think of graph paper or a spreadsheet.
grid.seen: No. 136 Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow; No. 147 Marilyn Diptych; No. 162 All-T’oqapu tunic.

ground line.def: A line, drawn or implied, that figures stand on. Ancient art often stacks several ground lines on top of each other.
ground line.think: Think of the line on lined notebook paper that your letters sit on.
ground line.seen: No. 13 Palette of King Narmer; No. 16 Standard of Ur; No. 24 Last judgment of Hu-Nefer.

hierarchical scale.def: Making the most important person the biggest, no matter where they stand in the scene. Size shows rank, not distance.
hierarchical scale.think: Think of a team photo where the coach is drawn twice as tall as the players.
hierarchical scale.seen: No. 13 Palette of King Narmer; No. 16 Standard of Ur; No. 169 Wall plaque from Oba’s palace.

hieratic.def: Stiff, formal, frontal and solemn, used for gods, rulers and holy figures to show they are above ordinary life.
hieratic.think: Think of royal guards standing perfectly still.
hieratic.seen: No. 18 King Menkaura and queen; No. 51 San Vitale; No. 54 Theotokos and Child.

highlight.def: The brightest spot on a surface, where light hits it most directly. Small highlights make things look shiny or wet.
highlight.think: Think of the white dot of light in someone’s eye in a photo.
highlight.seen: No. 92 Woman Holding a Balance; No. 68 The Arnolfini Portrait.

horizon line.def: The line where the land or sea seems to meet the sky. In linear perspective, the vanishing point usually sits on it, at the viewer’s eye level.
horizon line.think: Think of where the ocean meets the sky at the beach.
horizon line.seen: No. 83 Hunters in the Snow; No. 109 The Oxbow.

horror vacui.def: Filling every inch of a surface with figures or decoration so no empty space is left. Latin for ‘fear of empty space’.
horror vacui.think: Think of a bedroom wall completely covered in posters.
horror vacui.seen: No. 47 Ludovisi Battle Sarcophagus; No. 55 Lindisfarne Gospels carpet page.

hue.def: The plain name of a color: red, blue, green and so on.
hue.think: Think of the crayon’s name before you ask whether it is light or dark.

idealized.def: Showing people or things as more perfect than they really are: smooth, balanced, young and flawless, following a standard of beauty.
idealized.think: Think of a heavily retouched magazine cover.
idealized.seen: No. 34 Doryphoros; No. 43 Augustus of Prima Porta; No. 72 Birth of Venus; No. 27 Anavysos Kouros.

illusionism.def: Tricks that make a flat surface seem to have real depth, space or objects, so the wall or ceiling seems to open up.
illusionism.think: Think of a 3D street-art painting that looks like a hole in the sidewalk.
illusionism.seen: No. 39 House of the Vettii; No. 82 Il Gesù ceiling; No. 75 Sistine Chapel ceiling.

immersive.def: Surrounding the viewer with sound, image or space, so you feel you are inside the work rather than looking at it.
immersive.think: Like the difference between watching a movie on a phone and standing in the middle of it.

implied line.def: A line you do not actually see but your eye follows anyway, such as the direction of a pointing finger, a gaze, or a row of objects.
implied line.think: Think of how everyone turns to look when one person points at the sky.
implied line.seen: No. 85 Calling of Saint Matthew; No. 103 The Oath of the Horatii.

implied texture.def: Texture that is painted or drawn to look rough, soft or shiny, even though the actual surface is smooth.
implied texture.think: Think of a photo of a fuzzy sweater on a smooth phone screen.
implied texture.seen: No. 68 The Arnolfini Portrait; No. 96 Fruit and Insects.

interlace.def: A decoration of bands, ribbons or animal bodies that weave over and under each other in complicated knots.
interlace.think: Think of a Celtic knot or a tangle of braided cords.
interlace.seen: No. 55 Lindisfarne Gospels; No. 53 Merovingian looped fibulae.
interlace.see: zoomorphic, carpet page, horror vacui, arabesque.

intimate.def: Describes a work that feels private, smallscale or personal, as if you are seeing a quiet everyday moment.
intimate.think: Think of a candid photo rather than a posed group shot.
intimate.seen: No. 92 Woman Holding a Balance; No. 121 The Coiffure.

isocephaly.def: Lining up all the heads in a crowd at the same height, whether the figures are standing, riding or walking. It keeps a long frieze tidy.
isocephaly.think: Think of a class photo where everyone’s heads are level because of how they’re arranged.

line.def: A mark that is longer than it is wide. Lines can be straight, curved, thick, thin, calm or agitated, and they outline shapes, show movement or carry feeling.
line.think: Think of handwriting: the same words feel different in neat print and angry scrawl.
line.seen: No. 120 The Starry Night; No. 211 Great Wave; No. 132 Improvisation 28.

linear perspective.def: A math-based system for showing depth on a flat surface. Parallel lines (orthogonals) are drawn to meet at a vanishing point, and objects shrink as they recede. Developed in Renaissance Italy around 1420.
linear perspective.think: Think of railroad tracks that seem to meet far away.
linear perspective.seen: No. 73 Last Supper; No. 76 School of Athens.
linear perspective.see: onepoint perspective, orthogonal, vanishing point, horizon line.

linear style.def: A style that relies on clear outlines and sharp edges between forms, so shapes look crisp and polished. Often contrasted with a painterly style.
linear style.think: Think of a clean comic outline versus a smudgy watercolor.
linear style.seen: No. 107 La Grande Odalisque; No. 103 The Oath of the Horatii.

local color.def: The real, everyday color of an object in normal light, such as a lemon’s yellow or grass’s green.
local color.think: Think of the color you would name if someone asked ‘what color is a banana?’
local color.seen: No. 68 The Arnolfini Portrait; No. 96 Fruit and Insects.

matte.def: A flat, non-shiny surface, the opposite of glossy. On María Martínez’s black pots, matte painted designs stand out against the mirror-like polished areas.

medallion.def: A round or oval framed area holding a design or figure, often used as the central motif of carpets, ivories and ceilings.
medallion.seen: No. 57 Pyxis of al-Mughira; No. 191 Ardabil Carpet.

middle ground.def: The zone of a picture between the foreground and the background.
middle ground.think: Think of the middle row of a stadium crowd.
middle ground.seen: No. 83 Hunters in the Snow; No. 201 Travelers among Mountains and Streams.

modeling (shading).def: Using gradual light and shadow on a flat surface to make a form look rounded and three-dimensional.
modeling (shading).think: Think of shading a circle with a pencil until it looks like a ball.
modeling (shading).seen: No. 63 Arena Chapel, Lamentation; No. 92 Woman Holding a Balance.

monochrome.def: Made in one color, or in shades of a single color (including just black ink and grays). Also called monochromatic.
monochrome.seen: No. 227 Summer Trees; No. 229 A Book from the Sky.

monumental.def: Large, imposing and grand in feeling. A small object can still feel monumental if its forms are solid and powerful.
monumental.think: Think of standing at the bottom of a skyscraper.
monumental.seen: No. 201 Travelers among Mountains and Streams; No. 214 Moai on platform; No. 182 Buddha (Bamiyan).

motif.def: A repeated shape, figure or idea that shows up again and again in a work or style.
motif.think: Think of a catchy melody that returns throughout a song.
motif.seen: No. 5 Beaker with ibex motifs; No. 191 Ardabil Carpet.

movement.def: How a work suggests motion, or how it leads your eye around itself.
movement.think: Think of a blurred photo of a runner.
movement.seen: No. 117 The Horse in Motion; No. 37 Winged Victory of Samothrace; No. 120 The Starry Night.

multiple viewpoints.def: Showing an object or figure from several angles at once in one image, so it looks broken up or tilted. Key to Cubism and to Cézanne’s late paintings.
multiple viewpoints.think: Think of walking around a chair and drawing every side on one sheet.
multiple viewpoints.seen: No. 126 Les Demoiselles d’Avignon; No. 125 Mont Sainte-Victoire; No. 130 The Portuguese.

narrative.def: Art that tells a story or shows an event from a story.
narrative.think: Think of a movie still that makes you wonder what happens next.
narrative.seen: No. 59 Bayeux Tapestry; No. 203 Night Attack on the Sanjô Palace; No. 16 Standard of Ur.

naturalism.def: Showing things the way they actually look in the real world, with accurate details, proportions, light and texture.
naturalism.think: Think of a high-quality photo: no improvements, no simplifying.
naturalism.seen: No. 15 Seated scribe; No. 68 The Arnolfini Portrait; No. 96 Fruit and Insects; No. 41 Seated boxer.

negative space.def: The empty space around and between objects. Artists use it as an active part of the design, not just leftover background.
negative space.think: Think of the arrow hidden in the white space of the FedEx logo.
negative space.seen: No. 210 White and Red Plum Blossoms; No. 207 Ryoan-ji.
negative space.see: positive space, horror vacui, figure-ground relationship.

nonrepresentational.def: Art that shows no recognizable objects at all, only colors, lines and shapes. Also called nonobjective.
nonrepresentational.think: Think of a screensaver of moving colors.
nonrepresentational.seen: No. 136 Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow; No. 149 The Bay; No. 246 Stadia II.

nude.def: A human figure shown without clothes as a subject of art. The idealized nude was central to Greek and Renaissance art and was later challenged by artists like Manet and Kiki Smith.
nude.think: Art historians separate ‘naked’ (just unclothed) from ‘the nude’ (a long art tradition of ideal bodies).
nude.seen: No. 69 David (Donatello); No. 72 Birth of Venus; No. 242 Lying with the Wolf.
nude.see: idealized, Venus pudica, reclining nude, contrapposto.

oblique perspective.def: A way of showing depth used in Chinese and Japanese painting: the sides of buildings are drawn as parallel diagonal lines that never meet, so the scene can unroll sideways without one fixed viewpoint.
oblique perspective.think: Think of an isometric video game, where buildings are drawn at an angle but don’t shrink.
oblique perspective.seen: No. 203 Night Attack on the Sanjô Palace.

one-point perspective.def: Linear perspective in which all the receding lines meet at a single vanishing point.
one-point perspective.think: Think of standing in the middle of a long hallway.
one-point perspective.seen: No. 73 Last Supper; No. 76 School of Athens.

open form.def: A figure or sculpture whose limbs and parts reach out into the surrounding space instead of staying in one compact block.
open form.think: Think of a dancer leaping with arms flung wide.
open form.seen: No. 37 Winged Victory of Samothrace; No. 89 Ecstasy of Saint Teresa.
open form.see: closed form, dynamic, in the round.

organic.def: Irregular, curving shapes that look like they come from nature, such as leaves, waves or bodies. The opposite of geometric.
organic.think: Think of a puddle’s outline rather than a square.
organic.seen: No. 210 White and Red Plum Blossoms; No. 240 Guggenheim Museum Bilbao; No. 211 Great Wave.

orthogonal.def: In linear perspective, the diagonal lines (real or implied) that run back into the picture and meet at the vanishing point, such as the edges of a ceiling or floor tiles.
orthogonal.think: Think of the lines of a road or train tracks heading into the distance.
orthogonal.seen: No. 73 Last Supper; No. 76 School of Athens.
orthogonal.see: linear perspective, vanishing point, one-point perspective.

overlapping.def: Placing one thing partly in front of another. The one that blocks the other looks closer. It is the simplest way to show depth.
overlapping.think: Think of a stack of playing cards fanned in your hand.
overlapping.seen: No. 16 Standard of Ur; No. 63 Arena Chapel, Lamentation.

ovoid.def: Egg-shaped. In Northwest Coast art, the ovoid is a rounded, slightly squarish oval used as a basic building block of formline designs.
ovoid.seen: No. 164 Transformation mask; No. 217 Female deity (Nukuoro).

painterly.def: A style where you can see loose brushstrokes and soft edges, with color and texture more important than crisp outlines.
painterly.think: Think of a sketch done with quick, visible strokes instead of careful outlines.
painterly.seen: No. 120 The Starry Night; No. 145 Woman, I ; No. 116 The Saint-Lazare Station.

palette.def: The range of colors an artist uses in a work, for example a ‘limited palette’ or a ‘warm palette’. It is also the board on which a painter mixes paint.
palette.think: Think of the set of colors in a phone theme.
palette.seen: No. 136 Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow.

panoramic.def: A wide view showing a large stretch of land or city, as if you can turn your head and take it all in.
panoramic.think: Think of the panorama setting on your phone camera.
panoramic.seen: No. 109 The Oxbow; No. 118 The Valley of Mexico.

pathos.def: The quality that makes you feel pity, sadness or sympathy, usually through visible suffering or strong emotion.
pathos.think: Think of a movie scene that makes the whole theater go quiet.
pathos.seen: No. 38 Great Altar of Zeus and Athena at Pergamon; No. 41 Seated boxer; No. 62 Röttgen Pietà; No. 119 The Burghers of Calais.

pattern.def: A design made by repeating shapes, lines or colors in a regular way.
pattern.think: Think of wallpaper or a plaid shirt.
pattern.seen: No. 162 All-T’oqapu tunic; No. 191 Ardabil Carpet; No. 65 Alhambra.

picture plane.def: The flat front surface of a painting, which you can imagine as a window glass between you and the painted world.
picture plane.think: Think of the glass on an aquarium: the fish are behind it, but some art makes things seem to poke through it.
picture plane.seen: No. 82 Il Gesù ceiling; No. 126 Les Demoiselles d’Avignon.

positive space.def: The areas filled by the actual subject or solid parts of a work.
positive space.think: Think of the cookie, as opposed to the dough left over after you cut it out.

primary colors.def: Red, yellow and blue in traditional painting. They cannot be mixed from other paints, and they can be mixed to make most other colors.
primary colors.think: Think of the three basic paint tubes in a starter kit.
primary colors.seen: No. 136 Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow.

profile.def: A side view, especially of a face or figure, showing its outline.
profile.think: Think of a face on a coin.
profile.seen: No. 1 Apollo 11 Stones; No. 24 Last judgment of Hu-Nefer; No. 22 Akhenaton, Nefertiti, and three daughters.

proportion.def: The size of one part compared with another part or with the whole, such as head to body.
proportion.think: Think of a recipe ratio: two cups flour to one cup sugar.

psychological realism.def: Showing people’s inner emotions and states of mind truthfully, not just their outward appearance. Each of Rodin’s Burghers of Calais shows his own kind of despair.

pyramidal composition.def: Arranging figures so together they form a triangle, with the most important figure at the top. It feels stable and focused.
pyramidal composition.seen: No. 108 Liberty Leading the People; No. 73 Last Supper.

radial balance.def: Balance in which parts spread out evenly from a central point, like spokes of a wheel.
radial balance.think: Think of a pizza, a flower or a bicycle wheel.
radial balance.seen: No. 60 Chartres Cathedral (rose windows); No. 191 Ardabil Carpet.

realism.def: With a small r, it means showing things truthfully, including ugly or ordinary details. With a capital R, it names a 19th-century movement that painted everyday working people instead of heroes and myths.
realism.think: Think of a documentary rather than a fairy tale.
realism.seen: No. 113 The Stone Breakers; No. 41 Seated boxer.

register.def: One horizontal band in a work that is divided into stacked rows, like shelves. Each register often shows a different scene or level of importance.
register.think: Think of the rows on a bookshelf or panels in a comic page.
register.seen: No. 13 Palette of King Narmer; No. 16 Standard of Ur; No. 24 Last judgment of Hu-Nefer; No. 64 Golden Haggadah.

repetition.def: Using the same element again and again. It can create rhythm, unity or, in modern art, a sense of mass production.
repetition.think: Think of a row of identical soup cans on a supermarket shelf.
repetition.seen: No. 147 Marilyn Diptych; No. 250 Kui Hua Zi (Sunflower Seeds); No. 30 Apadana reliefs.

repoussoir.def: An object or figure placed at the very front edge of a picture, often dark and to one side, that pushes your eye back into the scene.
repoussoir.think: Think of a photographer framing a view with a tree branch in the corner.

representational.def: Art that shows recognizable things from the real world, whether realistic or stylized.
representational.think: If you can name what it is, it is representational.

rhythm.def: A sense of movement made by repeating elements at regular or changing intervals, the way a beat repeats in music.
rhythm.think: Think of fence posts flashing by from a car window.
rhythm.seen: No. 30 Audience Hall (apadana) reliefs; No. 35 Acropolis (Parthenon frieze).

saturation.def: How strong, pure or intense a color is. A highly saturated red is vivid; a low-saturation red is dull and grayish. Also called intensity or chroma.
saturation.think: Think of the saturation slider on a photo app.

scale.def: How big something is, either compared with us (a huge statue, a tiny figurine) or compared with other things in the same work.
scale.think: Think of a toy car versus a real car.
scale.seen: No. 182 Buddha (Bamiyan); No. 250 Kui Hua Zi (Sunflower Seeds); No. 150 Lipstick (Ascending) on Caterpillar Tracks.

schematic.def: Reduced to a simple, diagram-like set of basic shapes, giving the idea of something rather than its detailed look.
schematic.think: Think of the man and woman signs on restroom doors.
schematic.seen: No. 6 Anthropomorphic stele; No. 14 Votive figures from Eshnunna; No. 4 Running horned woman.

secondary colors.def: Orange, green and purple: the colors you get by mixing two primary colors.
secondary colors.think: Blue plus yellow gives green, like mixing two juice flavors.
secondary colors.see: primary colors, color wheel, complementary colors.

serene.def: Calm, peaceful and still in mood.
serene.think: Think of a quiet lake at dawn.
serene.seen: No. 71 Madonna and Child with Two Angels; No. 92 Woman Holding a Balance.

shade.def: A color made darker by adding black. (A tint is the lighter version, made by adding white.)
shade.think: Think of navy as a shade of blue.

shape.def: A flat, enclosed area with only height and width, such as a circle or a blob.
shape.think: Think of a cookie cutter outline.

shifting perspective.def: A Chinese way of painting landscape in which the viewer seems to move through the scene, seeing different parts from different heights instead of from one fixed spot.
shifting perspective.think: Think of a hike where you see the valley from below, then the peak from halfway up, all in one picture.
shifting perspective.seen: No. 201 Travelers among Mountains and Streams.
shifting perspective.see: multiple viewpoints, hanging scroll, atmospheric perspective.

silhouette.def: A shape filled in with one solid dark color, showing only the outline. Popular as cut-paper portraits in the 1700s and 1800s.
silhouette.think: Think of a black shadow cast on a wall.
silhouette.see: contour line, figure-ground relationship, cut paper.

space.def: The area around, between and within things. In a flat picture it means the illusion of depth; in sculpture and architecture it means the real air and room the work occupies.
space.think: Think of how deep a photo looks versus how deep a real room feels.
space.see: linear perspective, atmospheric perspective, overlapping, negative space.

static.def: Still and stable, with no suggested motion. Often achieved through vertical and horizontal lines and frontal poses.
static.think: Think of a parked car versus a racing one.
static.seen: No. 18 King Menkaura and queen; No. 14 Votive figures from Eshnunna.

stylized.def: Shown in a simplified, exaggerated or decorative way that follows a set style rather than copying nature exactly.
stylized.think: Think of a cartoon character: clearly a person, but drawn in a recognizable style.
stylized.seen: No. 9 Ambum Stone; No. 14 Votive figures from Eshnunna; No. 214 Moai on platform; No. 210 White and Red Plum Blossoms.

sublime.def: A feeling of awe mixed with fear in front of something overwhelming, like a storm, a huge mountain or the open sea. Romantic artists of the 1800s chased this feeling.
sublime.think: Think of standing at the edge of the Grand Canyon in a thunderstorm.
sublime.seen: No. 109 The Oxbow; No. 111 Slave Ship.

superimposition.def: Placing one image on top of another so they overlap, as when prehistoric painters added new animals over older ones on the same wall.
superimposition.seen: No. 2 Great Hall of the Bulls; No. 4 Running horned woman.

symmetry.def: When one half of a work mirrors the other across a center line. It feels orderly, stable and formal.
symmetry.think: Think of a butterfly’s wings or a human face.
symmetry.seen: No. 209 Taj Mahal; No. 191 Ardabil Carpet; No. 53 Merovingian looped fibulae.

tenebrism.def: An extreme form of chiaroscuro in which most of the picture is very dark and a few areas are hit by sharp, spotlight-like light. Associated with Caravaggio and his followers.
tenebrism.think: Think of a stage that is pitch black except for one spotlight.
tenebrism.seen: No. 85 Calling of Saint Matthew; No. 100 A Philosopher Giving a Lecture on the Orrery.

texture.def: How a surface feels, or looks like it would feel: rough, smooth, soft, bumpy, glossy. Actual texture can be touched; implied texture is only painted.
texture.think: Think of the difference between sandpaper and silk.
texture.seen: No. 138 Object (fur-covered cup); No. 120 The Starry Night; No. 245 Old Man’s Cloth.

theatricality.def: Staging a work like a dramatic scene in a play, with spotlights, emotional gestures and sometimes an ‘audience’ built in. Typical of Baroque art.
theatricality.think: Think of a big musical number with lighting cues.
theatricality.seen: No. 89 Ecstasy of Saint Teresa; No. 82 Il Gesù ceiling.

three-quarter view.def: A view of a face or figure turned partly away, halfway between frontal and profile, so you see one side more than the other.
three-quarter view.think: Think of most school portraits, with the head slightly turned.
three-quarter view.seen: No. 105 Self-Portrait (Vigée Le Brun); No. 68 The Arnolfini Portrait.

tint.def: A color made lighter by adding white.
tint.think: Think of pink as a tint of red.

trompe l’oeil.def: Painting so convincing that it fools you into thinking a painted thing is real. French for ‘fool the eye’.
trompe l’oeil.think: Think of a painted door on a wall that you try to open.
trompe l’oeil.seen: No. 82 Il Gesù ceiling; No. 39 House of the Vettii.
trompe l’oeil.see: illusionism, di sotto in sù, picture plane.

twisted perspective.def: Another name for composite view: showing a body or animal from different angles at once, such as horns seen from the front on a head seen from the side.
twisted perspective.think: Think of a cartoon where both eyes show even though the face is in profile.
twisted perspective.seen: No. 2 Great Hall of the Bulls; No. 13 Palette of King Narmer.

unity.def: The sense that all parts of a work belong together and make a complete whole.

value.def: How light or dark a color or tone is, from white through grays to black.
value.think: Think of turning a color photo to black-and-white: what’s left is value.

vanishing point.def: In linear perspective, the spot on the horizon line where receding parallel lines appear to meet and disappear. Artists often place something important there.
vanishing point.think: Think of where train tracks seem to join far away.
vanishing point.seen: No. 73 Last Supper (at Christ’s head); No. 76 School of Athens.
vanishing point.see: orthogonal, linear perspective, horizon line, focal point.

variety.def: Using differences in shape, color, size or texture to keep a work interesting. Usually balanced against unity.
variety.think: Think of a playlist that mixes fast and slow songs.

verism.def: Extreme, warts-and-all realism, especially in Roman Republican portraits that proudly show wrinkles, sagging skin and age as signs of wisdom and service.
verism.think: Think of a portrait with zero filters, on purpose.
verism.seen: No. 42 Head of a Roman patrician.

vertical perspective.def: A way of showing depth by placing things that are farther away higher up in the picture, rather than smaller.
vertical perspective.think: Think of a crowd photo taken from a balcony: people farther back appear higher in the frame.

viewpoint.def: The position from which the viewer seems to see the scene: low, high, straight on, from the side. Also called vantage point.
viewpoint.think: Think of where the camera is placed in a movie shot.
viewpoint.seen: No. 118 The Valley of Mexico; No. 121 The Coiffure.
viewpoint.see: bird’s-eye view, horizon line, multiple viewpoints.

visual weight.def: How strongly a part of a work pulls your attention. Big, dark, bright or busy areas feel heavier than small, pale or plain ones.
visual weight.think: Think of how one bright red sock stands out in a pile of gray laundry.

volume.def: The amount of three-dimensional space a form fills, or seems to fill in a painting.
volume.think: Think of how much water a vase could hold.
volume.seen: No. 63 Arena Chapel, Lamentation; No. 125 Mont Sainte-Victoire.

warm colors.def: Reds, oranges and yellows. They feel warm, energetic or emotional and tend to seem to come toward you.

zoomorphic.def: Shaped like an animal or using animal forms as decoration.
zoomorphic.seen: No. 3 Camelid sacrum in the shape of a canine; No. 53 Merovingian looped fibulae; No. 55 Lindisfarne Gospels.
zoomorphic.see: anthropomorphic, interlace, motif. 3 Painting, drawing and printmaking How flat images are made: the paints, the surfaces they go on, and the printing methods. If a question asks about materials or process for a painting, manuscript or print, the answer is in here.

acrylic paint.def: A fast-drying, waterbased paint made with plastic (synthetic polymer) binder, invented in the mid-1900s. It can be thinned like watercolor or used thick like oil.
acrylic paint.think: Think of the paint in a school craft kit, but artist quality.
acrylic paint.seen: No. 149 The Bay; No. 232 Dancing at the Louvre; No. 234 Earth’s Creation; No. 246 Stadia II.

action painting.def: A style of Abstract Expressionism (1940s and 1950s, New York) in which the painting records the artist’s energetic physical movements: big slashing, dripping or scrubbing brushstrokes.
action painting.think: Think of a painting as the footprint left behind by a dance.

album page.def: A single painting or sheet of calligraphy made to be mounted in an album, rather than to illustrate the text of a book. Persian, Mughal and Ottoman collectors gathered such pages into albums called muraqqa.
album page.think: Like one page in a royal collector’s scrapbook.
album page.seen: No. 208 Jahangir Preferring a Sufi Shaikh to Kings.

albumen print.def: An early photographic print (about 1850 to 1890) made on paper coated with egg white, which held the light-sensitive chemicals and gave a fine, glossy image.
albumen print.think: Egg white was the glue that held the picture on the paper.

altarpiece.def: A painted or carved work placed on or behind the altar of a church, showing holy figures or stories. Many have several hinged panels.
altarpiece.think: Think of the big picture behind the stage in a church, the one everyone faces.
altarpiece.seen: No. 66 Merode Altarpiece; No. 77 Isenheim altarpiece; No. 78 Entombment of Christ.

aquatint.def: A printmaking technique, related to etching, that uses acid eating through a powdered resin layer to make soft areas of tone that look like watercolor washes, instead of only lines.
aquatint.think: Think of shading in a print that looks grainy, like fine sandpaper.

binder.def: The sticky liquid that holds powdered color (pigment) together and makes it stick to a surface. The binder is what makes oil paint, tempera and acrylic different.
binder.think: Think of pigment as sand and binder as the glue that turns it into paint.

biombo.def: A Spanish word for a folding screen, borrowed from the Japanese ‘byōbu’. Biombos were made in colonial Mexico after Japanese screens arrived by trade.
biombo.think: The name itself shows the trade route: Japan to Mexico.
biombo.seen: No. 94 Screen with the Siege of Belgrade.

brocateado.def: A Spanish colonial painting technique of laying patterns of gold leaf over painted clothing to imitate rich brocade fabric. It makes the angels and saints of Andean painting glitter.
brocateado.see: gold leaf, Cuzco School, Viceregal art.

broken color.def: Painting with separate, unblended dabs of color placed side by side so they mix in the viewer’s eye instead of on the palette. A key Impressionist technique.
broken color.think: Up close it looks like confetti; step back and it turns into steam, sky or water.

brush and ink.def: The basic tools of East Asian painting and calligraphy: a soft, pointed brush and black ink ground from an ink stick. The same brushstrokes are used for writing and painting.
brush and ink.think: Think of a calligraphy pen that can also paint mountains.
brush and ink.seen: No. 201 Travelers among Mountains and Streams; No. 227 Summer Trees.

brushwork.def: The way paint is put on with a brush, and whether you can see the strokes. It can be smooth and invisible or thick, quick and expressive.
brushwork.think: Think of brushwork as an artist’s handwriting.
brushwork.seen: No. 120 The Starry Night; No. 145 Woman, I ; No. 125 Mont Sainte-Victoire.

buon fresco.def: True fresco: painting with water-based pigment onto wet lime plaster. As it dries, the color becomes part of the wall itself, so it lasts for centuries.
buon fresco.think: Think of dye soaking into wet cement and setting with it.
buon fresco.seen: No. 75 Sistine Chapel; No. 63 Arena Chapel; No. 143 Dream of a Sunday Afternoon.

burin.def: A small, sharp steel tool used to cut lines into a metal plate in engraving.
burin.think: Think of a tiny chisel that carves grooves in copper.
burin.seen: No. 74 Adam and Eve (Dürer); No. 106 Y no hai remedio.

byōbu.def: A Japanese folding screen made of hinged panels, often painted on gold-leafed paper, used to divide rooms and decorate homes.
byōbu.think: Think of a room divider that is also a giant painting.
byōbu.seen: No. 210 White and Red Plum Blossoms.

camera obscura.def: A dark box or room with a tiny hole or lens that projects an upsidedown image of the outside scene onto a wall or screen. Artists could trace it, and it led to the camera.
camera obscura.think: Latin for ‘dark room’. Think of a pinhole camera you can stand inside.

cangiante.def: Italian for ‘changing’. Painting the shadows of a fabric in a different, often lighter or brighter color instead of a darker shade of the same one, so the cloth seems to shimmer. Mannerists like Pontormo loved it.
cangiante.think: Like shot silk or a jacket that looks pink in one light and yellow in another.

canvas.def: A strong woven cloth, usually linen or cotton, stretched over a wooden frame and used as a surface for painting. It replaced wooden panels for most painting after the 1500s because it is lighter and can be rolled.
canvas.think: Think of a sturdy, tight drum skin made of fabric.
canvas.seen: No. 80 Venus of Urbino; No. 91 Las Meninas; No. 108 Liberty Leading the People.

caricature.def: A picture that exaggerates a person’s features or a group’s traits for comic or critical effect. Daumier mocked Nadar this way; Kara Walker turns racist caricatures back on their makers.
caricature.think: Like a boardwalk cartoon portrait with a giant head.
caricature.seen: No. 114 Nadar Raising Photography to the Height of Art; No. 243 Darkytown Rebellion.

carpet page.def: A full page in a medieval manuscript covered entirely in dense pattern, usually around a cross, with no text. It looks like a woven rug.
carpet page.think: Think of a page that is pure decoration, like a fancy bookmark page.

cartellino.def: A painted scrap of paper or small tablet in a picture, usually carrying the artist’s signature or a date, made to look as if it were really pinned or hanging there. Dürer hangs one on a branch in Adam and Eve.
cartellino.think: A painted sticky note with the artist’s name on it.

cartoon.def: In older art, a full-size preparatory drawing for a fresco, tapestry or painting. Its outlines were transferred to the wall by pricking holes and dusting charcoal through them.
cartoon.think: Think of a stencil sketch made before the real thing.

cartouche.def: A decorative frame, often shaped like a scroll or shield, that holds an inscription. In Egyptian art the word means the oval loop drawn around a pharaoh’s name.

casein.def: A paint whose binder is made from milk protein. It dries quickly to a flat, matte finish.
casein.seen: No. 141 The Migration of the Negro, Panel no. 49.

casta painting.def: A type of painting from colonial Mexico (1700s) showing families of mixed racial background in sets, each labeled with a category name. They recorded a colonial system of racial ranking.
casta painting.think: Think of a chart that tries to label and rank people by ancestry.
casta painting.seen: No. 97 Spaniard and Indian Produce a Mestizo.

charcoal.def: Burnt wood (or bone) used as a black drawing material. One of the oldest art materials.
charcoal.think: Think of the black stuff left in a campfire, used as a crayon.

chronophotography.def: Taking a quick series of photos of something moving to study each stage of its motion. Pioneered by Eadweard Muybridge.
chronophotography.think: Think of burst mode on your phone.

collage.def: A work made by gluing paper, photos, fabric or other materials onto a flat surface. From the French ‘coller’, to glue.
collage.think: Think of a scrapbook page or a vision board.

colophon.def: A note at the end of a book or scroll recording who made it, when, or who later admired it. In Chinese scrolls, later owners and viewers often added their own colophons.
colophon.think: Think of the comments section added after a post.

colorito.def: Italian for ‘coloring’. The Venetian approach of building a painting through rich color and soft brushwork rather than precise drawing. Titian is the classic example; it is the opposite of disegno.

composite image.def: A picture built by combining parts from different sources or moments into one. Rachel Ruysch gathered flowers that never bloomed at the same time into one bouquet; Mariko Mori digitally combined photos of herself with a landscape.
composite image.think: Like a photoshopped picture, long before Photoshop.
composite image.seen: No. 96 Fruit and Insects; No. 241 Pure Land.

cross-hatching.def: Shading made by drawing sets of fine parallel lines that cross each other. The closer the lines, the darker the area.
cross-hatching.think: Think of a tic-tac-toe grid repeated very small to make a shadow.

cut paper.def: Shapes cut out of paper and arranged or pasted as a work of art. Kara Walker uses large black cut-paper silhouettes on white walls.
cut paper.think: Think of paper snowflakes, but telling a story.

daguerreotype.def: The first widely used photographic process (announced 1839). It made one single, mirror-like image on a polished silver-coated copper plate, with no negative, so it could not be copied.
daguerreotype.think: Think of a oneof-a-kind photo printed on a tiny mirror.

dedication page.def: A page at the start of a manuscript that shows or names the patron for whom the book was made.
dedication page.think: Think of a ‘This book is dedicated to...’ page, with a portrait.

di sotto in sù.def: Painting a ceiling so the figures look as if you are seeing them from directly below, floating in real space above you. Italian for ‘from below to above’.
di sotto in sù.think: Think of lying on the grass looking up at people on a balcony.

digital photography.def: Photography that records images as computer data instead of on film, which makes pictures easy to edit and combine. Mariko Mori used digital tools to build Pure Land.

diptych.def: A work made of two panels, often hinged together.
diptych.think: Think of a two-page spread in a book.

disegno.def: Italian for both ‘drawing’ and ‘design’. The Florentine and Roman belief that great art begins with drawing and careful intellectual planning, praised in artists like Michelangelo. It was debated against Venetian colorito.
disegno.think: Disegno is the blueprint; colorito is the paint job. Renaissance critics argued over which mattered more.

disguised symbolism.def: Ordinary objects in a realistic scene that quietly carry religious meaning, a hallmark of Northern Renaissance painting. In the Merode Altarpiece, the lilies, candle and washbasin all point to Mary’s purity.
disguised symbolism.think: Easter eggs hidden in plain sight.
disguised symbolism.seen: No. 66 Merode Altarpiece; No. 68 The Arnolfini Portrait.

dot painting.def: A style of contemporary Aboriginal Australian painting built up from many dabs or dots of color, connected to body painting and ceremonial designs about ancestral land.
dot painting.think: Think of millions of colored dots that together map a place and its stories.

drawing.def: Making marks on a surface with a tool like pencil, charcoal, chalk or ink, usually emphasizing line. Drawings can be finished works or sketches for later projects.
drawing.think: Think of everything from a doodle to an architect’s plan.
drawing.seen: No. 242 Lying with the Wolf ; No. 1 Apollo 11 Stones.

drypoint.def: An intaglio printmaking method where the artist scratches lines straight into a metal plate with a sharp needle. The scratch throws up a rough edge (burr) that prints soft, velvety lines.
drypoint.think: Think of scratching a design into a smooth metal surface with a nail.
drypoint.seen: No. 121 The Coiffure; No. 106 Y no hai remedio.

easel painting.def: A painting made on a portable support, like canvas or panel, that can be moved and hung anywhere, as opposed to a mural fixed to a wall.
easel painting.think: Think of a framed painting you could carry out the door.

edition.def: The total set of prints made from one block or plate at one time. Each sheet in it is an impression.
edition.think: Think of a limited-edition sneaker drop: a fixed number made from the same design.

emaki.def: Short for emakimono: a Japanese illustrated handscroll that combines pictures and text to tell a story, unrolled section by section from right to left.
emaki.think: A comic strip on a roll, read one arm’s length at a time.
emaki.seen: No. 203 Night Attack on the Sanjô Palace.

en plein air.def: Painting outdoors, directly in front of the subject, instead of in a studio. Made easier in the 1800s by paint in portable tubes. French for ‘in the open air’.
en plein air.think: Think of setting up an easel in a field instead of working from a photo.

encaustic.def: Painting with pigment mixed into hot melted wax. The colors stay bright and glossy for centuries. Used for Roman-Egyptian mummy portraits and early icons.
encaustic.think: Think of painting with melted crayons.

enconchado.def: A kind of painting from colonial Mexico with pieces of mother-ofpearl set into the surface under the paint, so it shimmers. It was inspired by Asian lacquerware with shell inlay.
enconchado.think: Think of a painting with sparkly shell pieces built in.

engraving.def: An intaglio print made by cutting lines into a metal plate with a burin, filling the grooves with ink, wiping the surface clean and pressing paper onto it. It gives sharp, precise lines.
engraving.think: Think of a dollar bill: its fine lines come from engraving.

etching.def: An intaglio print made by drawing through a wax coating on a metal plate, then dipping the plate in acid, which eats lines into the exposed metal. The lines can be looser and more sketch-like than engraving.
etching.think: Think of drawing in wax and letting acid do the cutting for you.
etching.seen: No. 87 Self-Portrait with Saskia; No. 106 Y no hai remedio.

exposure.def: In photography, letting light reach the film, plate or sensor for a set time to record an image. Early photos needed long exposures, so moving things blurred; Muybridge used very fast exposures to freeze a running horse.
exposure.seen: No. 110 Still Life in Studio; No. 117 The Horse in Motion.

folding screen.def: A free-standing set of hinged panels, often painted, used to divide space in a room.
folding screen.think: Think of a changing screen in an old movie.
folding screen.seen: No. 210 White and Red Plum Blossoms; No. 94 Screen with the Siege of Belgrade.

folio.def: A single sheet or page of a manuscript or book. Folios are numbered with r (recto, the front) and v (verso, the back).
folio.think: Think of one leaf of a notebook, both sides.
folio.seen: No. 187 Folio from a Qur’an; No. 81 Codex Mendoza.

freehand painting.def: Painting a design directly by hand, without stencils, stamps or rubbing boards. Niuean hiapo stands out because its fine, dense patterns were painted freehand.

fresco.def: Painting on plaster on a wall or ceiling. In true (buon) fresco the plaster is still wet; in fresco secco it is dry.
fresco.think: Italian for ‘fresh’, as in freshly laid plaster.
fresco.seen: No. 75 Sistine Chapel; No. 63 Arena Chapel; No. 32 Tomb of the Triclinium; No. 39 House of the Vettii.
fresco.see: buon fresco, fresco secco, mural, giornata.

fresco secco.def: Painting on dry plaster with paint that has its own binder. It allows more detail and colors but flakes off over time. Leonardo’s Last Supper used an experimental drywall method, which is why it began decaying in his own lifetime.
fresco secco.think: Think of painting on a finished wall instead of letting the color set with it.

frontispiece.def: A picture placed facing the title page at the start of a book.
frontispiece.think: Think of the full-page picture right inside the cover of an old book.

gelatin silver print.def: The standard black-and-white photographic print of the 1900s, made on paper coated with light-sensitive silver salts held in gelatin.

genre scene.def: A painting of ordinary people doing everyday things, like working, cooking or chatting.
genre scene.think: Think of a slice-of-life scene instead of a superhero movie.
genre scene.seen: No. 92 Woman Holding a Balance; No. 83 Hunters in the Snow; No. 113 The Stone Breakers.

gesso.def: A white mix of chalk or plaster and glue brushed onto wood panels or canvas to make a smooth, bright surface for painting.
gesso.think: Think of primer paint on a wall before the real color.

gestural.def: Describes loose, energetic brushwork that records the movement of the artist’s hand and arm. It is a hallmark of Abstract Expressionism and Neo-Expressionism.
gestural.think: You can almost see the artist’s arm swinging.
gestural.seen: No. 145 Woman, I ; No. 226 Horn Players.

giornata.def: The patch of fresh plaster a fresco painter could finish in one day before it dried. Plural: giornate. You can sometimes see the seams between days.
giornata.seen: No. 75 Sistine Chapel; No. 63 Arena Chapel.

glaze (oil painting).def: A thin, see-through layer of oil paint laid over another dry layer. Many glazes build up glowing, jewel-like color and deep shadows.
glaze (oil painting).think: Think of colored cellophane layered over a picture.
glaze (oil painting).seen: No. 68 The Arnolfini Portrait; No. 66 Merode Altarpiece.

gloss.def: A note written in the margin or between the lines of a text to explain or translate it. Spanish glosses label the Aztec pictures in the Codex Mendoza.

gold ground.def: A background covered with gold leaf instead of a landscape or room, making holy figures seem to exist in heaven rather than on earth.
gold ground.think: Think of a portrait set against a glowing golden wall instead of a view.
gold ground.seen: No. 54 Theotokos and Child; No. 61 Bible moralisée dedication page.

gold leaf.def: Gold hammered into sheets thinner than tissue paper and applied to a surface to make it shine.
gold leaf.think: Think of a golden sticker so thin you could see light through it.
gold leaf.seen: No. 128 The Kiss (Klimt); No. 64 Golden Haggadah; No. 210 White and Red Plum Blossoms; No. 61 Bible moralisée.

gouache.def: Opaque watercolor: water-based paint with extra white or chalk added so it covers what is underneath, drying flat and matte.

graﬀiti.def: Words or images scrawled or spray-painted on public walls. Jean-Michel Basquiat began as the graﬀiti writer SAMO and brought its rough, word-filled look into his paintings.

graphite.def: The soft gray carbon inside an ordinary pencil, used for drawing.
graphite.think: It is literally pencil ‘lead’ (which contains no lead).

grisaille.def: Painting done entirely in shades of gray, often to imitate stone sculpture.
grisaille.think: Think of a black-and-white painting meant to look like a carved statue.

ground.def: The prepared layer put on a support before painting, such as gesso on a panel. In etching it is the wax coating on the plate.

group portrait.def: A portrait of several people together, such as a family, a royal court or the members of a guild.

handscroll.def: A long horizontal scroll, sometimes many feet long, unrolled from right to left a section at a time while held in the hands. Used in China, Japan and Korea for stories and landscapes.
handscroll.think: Think of scrolling through a long panorama photo bit by bit.
handscroll.seen: No. 203 Night Attack on the Sanjô Palace.

hanging scroll.def: A vertical scroll painting mounted on silk or paper with a rod at the bottom, made to hang on a wall and be rolled up for storage.
hanging scroll.think: Think of a poster that rolls up like a window shade.
hanging scroll.seen: No. 201 Travelers among Mountains and Streams; No. 205 Portrait of Sin Sukju.

hardboard.def: A thin, stiff board made of compressed wood fibers, used as a cheap painting surface. Jacob Lawrence painted his Migration Series on hardboard panels.
hardboard.seen: No. 141 The Migration of the Negro, Panel no. 49.

hatching.def: Shading made with many fine parallel lines close together.
hatching.think: Think of quick diagonal pencil strokes used to darken a sketch.

hide painting.def: Painting on animal skin. Plains and Plateau peoples of North America painted hides to record histories, events and visions.
hide painting.think: Think of a deer or elk skin used as a canvas.

history painting.def: In the European academic system, large paintings of important stories from history, myth, religion or literature, meant to teach a moral lesson. It was ranked the highest kind of painting.
history painting.think: Think of a blockbuster epic, ranked above a family photo or a fruit bowl.
history painting.seen: No. 103 The Oath of the Horatii; No. 108 Liberty Leading the People.

ignudo.def: Italian for ‘nude’. One of the twenty muscular nude young men Michelangelo painted on the Sistine Chapel ceiling, seated at the corners of the smaller Genesis scenes. Plural: ignudi.

illuminated manuscript.def: A handwritten book decorated with painted pictures, colored letters and often gold or silver. Before printing, every book was made by hand.
illuminated manuscript.think: Think of a hand-copied book where the pages literally glow with gold.
illuminated manuscript.seen: No. 50 Vienna Genesis; No. 55 Lindisfarne Gospels; No. 61 Bible moralisée; No. 64 Golden Haggadah.

impasto.def: Paint laid on so thickly that it stands up from the surface and shows the marks of the brush or knife.
impasto.think: Think of thick frosting swirled on a cake.

impression.def: One single print pulled from a block or plate. Early impressions are often the sharpest.
impression.think: Think of one stamp of a rubber stamp.

improvisation.def: Making something up on the spot, like a jazz musician. Kandinsky called a group of his paintings Improvisations because they came from spontaneous inner feeling rather than planning.

incipit page.def: The decorated opening page of a book or chapter in a manuscript, where the first words are made huge and ornamental. From the Latin for ‘it begins’.
incipit page.think: Think of a giant fancy first letter at the start of a fairy tale.

ink.def: A dark liquid for writing, drawing and painting. In East Asia, ink is made from soot and glue pressed into a stick and ground with water on a stone.
ink.think: Think of what fills a fountain pen.
ink.seen: No. 201 Travelers among Mountains and Streams; No. 227 Summer Trees; No. 242 Lying with the Wolf.

inscription.def: Words written, painted or carved on a work, such as a title, poem, name or dedication.
inscription.think: Think of a message engraved on the back of a watch.
inscription.seen: No. 19 Code of Hammurabi; No. 57 Pyxis of al-Mughira; No. 188 Basin (Baptistère de St. Louis).

intaglio.def: The family of printmaking methods where lines are cut or etched into a metal plate. Ink sits in the grooves, and strong pressure pulls it onto paper. Engraving, etching, drypoint and aquatint are all intaglio.
intaglio.think: Think of the opposite of a rubber stamp: the ink lives in the low parts, not the high parts.
intaglio.seen: No. 74 Adam and Eve (engraving); No. 87 Self-Portrait with Saskia (etching); No. 121 The Coiffure.

key block.def: In color woodblock printing, the block carved with the main black outlines. The separate color blocks are cut to line up with it.
key block.think: The coloring-book outline that all the colors fill in.

Kufic.def: An early, angular style of Arabic script with straight lines and sharp corners, used in the first centuries of Islam for copying the Qur’an and in architecture.
Kufic.think: Think of a blocky font compared with flowing cursive.

labors of the months.def: A medieval series of images showing the typical work of each month, such as plowing, harvesting and hunting, common in calendars, prayer books and church carvings.

landscape.def: A picture whose main subject is natural scenery: land, sky, trees and water. It was a major subject in China by the 900s and became one in Europe from the 1500s.
landscape.seen: No. 83 Hunters in the Snow; No. 109 The Oxbow; No. 118 The Valley of Mexico; No. 201 Travelers among Mountains and Streams.
landscape.see: monumental landscape, shanshui, Hudson River School, atmospheric perspective.

letterpress.def: Printing with raised metal or wooden letters that are inked and pressed onto paper. It could be combined with woodcut pictures on the same page.
letterpress.think: Think of a typewriter, but the whole page at once.
letterpress.seen: No. 79 Allegory of Law and Grace.

lithograph.def: A print made by drawing with a greasy crayon on a flat stone or metal plate. The surface is wet, so greasy ink sticks only to the drawing (oil and water don’t mix). Invented about 1796.
lithograph.think: Think of drawing with a crayon, then using the oil-and-water trick to print it.
lithograph.seen: No. 114 Nadar Raising Photography to the Height of Art; No. 212 Chairman Mao en Route to Anyuan.

manuscript.def: A book or document written by hand. Before printing, every book was a manuscript, and luxury ones were richly painted.
manuscript.seen: No. 55 Lindisfarne Gospels; No. 64 Golden Haggadah; No. 189 Bahram Gur Fights the Karg; No. 190 The Court of Gayumars.

matrix.def: The block, plate, stone or screen that holds the image in printmaking and is inked to make each print.
matrix.think: Think of the stamp, as opposed to the stamped paper.

medium.def: The material an artist uses, such as oil paint, marble or ink. Plural: media. ‘Mixed media’ means several materials combined.
medium.think: Think of what the art is made out of.

meritorious subject portrait.def: A Korean Joseon court portrait ordered by the king to honor an oﬀicial for loyal service. It shows the sitter in full oﬀicial robes, often with a rank badge.
meritorious subject portrait.think: A painted ‘employee of the year’ award from the king.

mineral pigment.def: Color made by grinding up colored rocks and earth, such as red and yellow ochre or black manganese. The oldest paints.
mineral pigment.think: Think of crushing colored chalk or clay into powder.
mineral pigment.seen: No. 2 Great Hall of the Bulls; No. 4 Running horned woman.

miniature.def: A small, detailed painting, often in a book or album. In the Persian and Mughal worlds, miniatures were made with fine brushes, bright opaque color and gold.
miniature.think: Think of a painting so detailed you need to lean in close.
miniature.seen: No. 189 Bahram Gur Fights the Karg; No. 190 The Court of Gayumars; No. 208 Jahangir Preferring a Sufi Shaikh to Kings.
miniature.see: opaque watercolor, illuminated manuscript, vertical perspective.

modern moral subject.def: William Hogarth’s name for his painted and printed series that mocked the bad behavior of his own day, such as greed, vanity and loveless marriages for money, to teach a moral lesson.
modern moral subject.think: A soap opera with a moral, told in pictures.
modern moral subject.seen: No. 98 The Tête à Tête (Marriage à la Mode).

modulation.def: Gradual shifts in color or tone. Cézanne built up forms through color modulation, setting warm and cool patches side by side instead of using light-and-dark shading.

monumental landscape.def: A Northern Song Chinese style of landscape painting with towering central mountains that dwarf tiny human figures, expressing the grandeur and order of nature.
monumental landscape.seen: No. 201 Travelers among Mountains and Streams.

movable type.def: Individual letters or characters made as separate pieces that can be arranged into text, printed, and then reused.
movable type.think: Think of Scrabble tiles that you can rearrange to print new words.
movable type.seen: No. 79 Allegory of Law and Grace; No. 229 A Book from the Sky.

mural.def: A large painting done directly on a wall or ceiling.
mural.think: Think of street art covering the side of a building.
mural.seen: No. 143 Dream of a Sunday Afternoon in the Alameda Park; No. 75 Sistine Chapel.

muraqqa.def: A Persian, Mughal or Ottoman album that collected paintings and samples of calligraphy, often set in decorated borders, for a royal or elite collector.
muraqqa.seen: No. 208 Jahangir Preferring a Sufi Shaikh to Kings.

Mylar.def: A thin, tough, smooth plastic film. Some contemporary artists paint and collage on it instead of paper or canvas.
Mylar.think: Think of the shiny material in party balloons, in a matte form.

mythological painting.def: A painting of stories from Greek and Roman myths. In the Renaissance, myths like Botticelli’s Birth of Venus were also read as ideas about beauty and love.

narrative series.def: A set of paintings or prints that tell a story in order, like chapters in a book. Hogarth’s Marriage A-la-Mode and Jacob Lawrence’s sixty Migration Series panels are examples.
narrative series.seen: No. 98 The Tête à Tête (Marriage à la Mode); No. 141 The Migration of the Negro, Panel no. 49.
narrative series.see: series, modern moral subject, continuous narrative.

negative.def: In photography, developed film or a glass plate on which light and dark are reversed. Shining light through it makes positive prints, so many copies can come from one negative. A daguerreotype, by contrast, is a one-of-a-kind image with no negative.

odalisque.def: A woman in an Ottoman harem; in European painting, a reclining nude in an imagined ‘Oriental’ setting, a favorite subject of Orientalism.

oil paint.def: Paint made with pigment mixed in a drying oil, usually linseed oil. It dries slowly, so artists can blend smoothly and build up thin glazes; it became the main European painting medium by the 1500s.
oil paint.think: Think of a paint that stays wet long enough to keep fixing it for days.
oil paint.seen: No. 68 The Arnolfini Portrait; No. 66 Merode Altarpiece; No. 80 Venus of Urbino.

oil paintstick.def: Oil paint formed into a solid stick, like a giant crayon, so artists can draw directly with paint. Basquiat used it in Horn Players.

oil sketch.def: A quick, small oil painting made to plan a larger work. Rubens planned big projects such as the Marie de’ Medici Cycle (No. 86) with oil sketches that his workshop then enlarged.

opaque watercolor.def: Water-based paint thick enough to cover what is underneath, used for Persian and Mughal miniatures. Similar to gouache.
opaque watercolor.think: Think of watercolor you can’t see through.
opaque watercolor.seen: No. 189 Bahram Gur Fights the Karg; No. 190 The Court of Gayumars.

palimpsest.def: Originally a manuscript page scraped clean and written over, with traces of the old writing still visible. In art, any surface where earlier layers show through later ones.

panel.def: A flat board, usually wood, used as a surface to paint on. Before canvas took over, most European paintings were on panels.
panel.think: Think of painting on a tabletop or a cabinet door.
panel.seen: No. 66 Merode Altarpiece; No. 68 The Arnolfini Portrait; No. 54 Theotokos and Child.

papyrus.def: A paper-like writing surface made in ancient Egypt by pressing together strips of the papyrus reed. The word ‘paper’ comes from it.
papyrus.think: Think of a woven mat of plant stems flattened into a sheet.

parchment.def: Animal skin (usually sheep or goat) soaked, scraped, stretched and dried to make a smooth, tough writing surface. Fine calfskin parchment is called vellum.
parchment.think: Think of a very thin, stiff leather page.

passage.def: A technique, used by Cézanne and the Cubists, of leaving edges open so one plane flows into the next, blurring the boundaries between objects and space.

pastel.def: Sticks of powdered pigment held together with a little binder, used like chalk. Pastel gives soft, powdery, bright color.

photography.def: Making images by capturing light on a light-sensitive surface. Since the 1830s it has been used both to record facts and as an art form.
photography.think: Think of what your phone camera does, invented with chemicals and glass instead of chips.
photography.seen: No. 117 The Horse in Motion; No. 127 The Steerage; No. 231 Untitled, History Portraits; No. 241 Pure Land.
photography.see: daguerreotype, albumen print, staged photography, camera obscura.

photogravure.def: A printing process that transfers a photograph onto a metal plate etched with acid, then prints it in ink, giving rich, velvety tones.
photogravure.think: Think of a photo turned into an etching.

photomontage.def: A collage made of cut and combined photographs, arranged to make a new, often political image. Popular in Soviet and Dada art of the 1920s and 1930s.
photomontage.think: Think of a meme made by pasting photos together.
photomontage.seen: No. 137 The Results of the First Five-Year Plan.

pigment.def: Colored powder that gives paint its color. Pigments come from minerals, plants, insects, or (since the 1800s) chemistry labs.
pigment.think: Think of the powder in a packet of drink mix before you add water.
pigment.seen: No. 2 Great Hall of the Bulls.

plate.def: The flat piece of metal (usually copper) into which an image is cut or etched for intaglio printing. Also a single full-page picture in a book.
plate.think: Think of the metal stamp a print is pulled from.

polyptych.def: A work made of many panels, often hinged, usually more than three. Large altarpieces are often polyptychs.
polyptych.think: Think of a fold-out map with lots of sections.

posthumous portrait.def: A portrait made after the sitter’s death, from memory, earlier images or descriptions. Cabrera’s Sor Juana and Lindauer’s Tamati Waka Nene are examples.
posthumous portrait.seen: No. 99 Portrait of Sor Juana; No. 220 Tamati Waka Nene.

predella.def: The long, low strip of small paintings along the bottom of an altarpiece, often showing extra scenes.
predella.think: Think of the footnotes at the bottom of a page.

print source.def: A printed image, such as an engraving, that an artist copied or adapted. Colonial painters in the Americas often worked from European prints, so poses and compositions traveled across the ocean.

printmaking.def: Making images that can be repeated by transferring ink from a prepared surface (block, plate, stone or screen) onto paper. The main families are relief, intaglio, lithography and screenprinting.
printmaking.think: Think of a stamp: one design, many copies.

projection.def: Light thrown onto a wall or screen from a projector, used by some contemporary artists as part of an installation, so viewers’ shadows can join the scene.
projection.think: Think of an overhead projector in class.

reclining nude.def: A nude figure lying on a couch or bed, a long-running European art type from Titian’s Venus of Urbino to Ingres’s Grande Odalisque and Manet’s Olympia, later reworked by artists like Kiki Smith and Wangechi Mutu.
reclining nude.seen: No. 80 Venus of Urbino; No. 107 La Grande Odalisque; No. 115 Olympia; No. 247 Preying Mantra.
reclining nude.see: nude, odalisque, male gaze, Venus pudica.

relief print.def: A print made by carving away the parts of a block that should stay blank, then inking the raised parts left standing. Woodcuts and woodblock prints are relief prints.
relief print.think: Think of a rubber stamp: the raised parts print.
relief print.seen: No. 79 Allegory of Law and Grace; No. 134 Memorial Sheet for Karl Liebknecht; No. 211 Great Wave.

retablo.def: Spanish for ‘altarpiece’. In Mexico it also means a small devotional painting on tin thanking a saint for a miracle. Frida Kahlo borrowed the look of these folk paintings.

rock art.def: Paintings (pictographs) or carvings (petroglyphs) made on cave walls, cliffs or stones. The earliest surviving art.
rock art.think: Think of the first walls people ever decorated.
rock art.seen: No. 2 Great Hall of the Bulls; No. 4 Running horned woman; No. 1 Apollo 11 Stones.

roundel.def: A circular frame or medallion containing a picture or design.
roundel.think: Think of a picture in a round locket.
roundel.see: dedication page, illuminated manuscript, stained glass.

screenprint.def: A print made by forcing ink through a fine mesh screen with a stencil blocking some areas. Andy Warhol used it with photographs to make art look mass-produced. Also called silkscreen.
screenprint.think: Think of how custom T-shirts are printed.

scroll.def: A long roll of papyrus, paper or silk with writing or images, unrolled to read and rolled up to store.
scroll.think: Think of a treasure map rolled up with a ribbon.
scroll.seen: No. 24 Last judgment of Hu-Nefer; No. 203 Night Attack on the Sanjô Palace; No. 205 Portrait of Sin Sukju.
